text: A square loop of area 25 cm${}^{2}$ has a resistance of 10 $\Omega$. The loop is placed in uniform magnetic field of magnitude 40.0 T. The plane of loop is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in pulling the loop out of the magnetic field slowly and uniformly in 1.0 sec, will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given $B=40.0\text{T}$, $A=25\text{cm}^{2}=25\times 10^{-4}\text{m}^{2}$, $R=10\Omega$ and $t=1.0\text{s}$.

Pulling the loop out uniformly reduces the flux from $BA$ to zero at a steady rate, so the induced emf is

$ε=\dfrac{\Delta 𝜙}{\Delta t}=\dfrac{40\times 25\times 10^{-4}}{1.0}=0.1\text{V}$

The pull is slow and uniform, so there is no change in kinetic energy and the work done equals the heat produced in the loop:

$W=\dfrac{ε^{2}}{R}t=\dfrac{(0.1)^{2}}{10}\times 1.0=1.0\times 10^{-3}\text{J}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Heat energy of 184 kJ is given to ice of mass 600 g at $-12^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$. Specific heat of ice is $2222.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{kg}^{-1^{\circ }}\mathrm{C}^{-1}$ and latent heat of ice is 336 $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{kg}^{-1}$

A. Final temperature of system will be 0${}^{\circ }$C.

B. Final temperature of the system will be greater than 0${}^{\circ }$C.

C. The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of 5 : 1.

D. The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of 1 : 5.

E. The final system will have water only.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Heat required to raise the temperature of ice to 0${}^{\circ }$C is

$=\frac{600}{1000}(2222.3)(12)$

$=16000.5$ J

$\approx 16$ kJ

Heat required to melt ice completely

$=\left (\frac{600}{1000}\right )(336)$ kJ

$=201.6$ kJ

Energy left $=(184-16)=168$ kJ

$\therefore$ Partial ice will melt

$\therefore$ $168=(m_{icemelted})336$

$0.5$ kg $=(m_{icemelted})$

$\therefore$ $m_{ice}:m_{water}=1:5$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Identify the correct statements from the following :

A. Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative.

B. Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative.

C. Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive.

D. Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is zero.

E. Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum is negative.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Work done by a force is $W=Fs\cos θ$: positive when the force has a component along the displacement, negative when it opposes the displacement.

A: The man pulls the rope upward and the bucket moves upward, so the work done by the man is positive; A is incorrect.

B: Gravity acts downward while the bucket moves upward, so the work done by gravity is negative; B is correct.

C: Friction acts up the incline while the body slides down, so the work done by friction is negative; C is incorrect.

D: At uniform velocity the applied force balances friction and acts along the motion, so it does positive work $Fs$; only the net work is zero, because friction does $-Fs$. D is incorrect.

E: Air resistance always opposes the velocity of the bob, so its work is negative; E is correct.

The correct statements are B and E only.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: An object moves at a constant speed along a circular path in a horizontal plane with center at the origin. When the object is at $x=+2\mathrm{m}$, its velocity is $-4\hat{\mathrm{j}}$ m/s. The object's velocity (v) and acceleration (a) at $x=-2\mathrm{m}$ will be
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$a=\dfrac{v^{2}}{R}=\dfrac{16}{2}=8\text{m s}^{-2}\Rightarrow ⃗{a}=8\hat{i}\text{m s}^{-2}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A fully loaded boeing aircraft has a mass of $5.4\times 10^{5}$ kg. Its total wing area is 500 m${}^{2}$. It is in level flight with a speed of 1080  km/h. If the density of air $ρ$ is 1.2 kg m${}^{-3}$, the fractional increase in the speed of the air on the upper surface of the wing relative to the lower surface in percentage will be. ($\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Speed of the aircraft: $v=1080\text{km h}^{-1}=300\text{m s}^{-1}$.

In level flight the pressure difference between the lower and upper surfaces of the wings supports the weight:

$\Delta P=\dfrac{mg}{A}=\dfrac{5.4\times 10^{5}\times 10}{500}=1.08\times 10^{4}\text{Pa}$

By Bernoulli's principle, with $v_{u}$ and $v_{l}$ the air speeds over the upper and lower surfaces and $v_{av}=\dfrac{v_{u}+v_{l}}{2}\approx 300\text{m s}^{-1}$,

$\Delta P=\dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left (v_{u}^{2}-v_{l}^{2}\right )=ρv_{av}(v_{u}-v_{l})$

$\dfrac{v_{u}-v_{l}}{v_{av}}=\dfrac{\Delta P}{ρv_{av}^{2}}=\dfrac{1.08\times 10^{4}}{1.2\times (300)^{2}}=0.1$

The fractional increase in speed is $0.1$, that is $10%$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
At 300 K, the rms speed of oxygen molecules is $\sqrt{\frac{α+5}{α}}$ times to that of its average speed in the gas. Then, the value of $α$ will be

(used $π=\frac{22}{7}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a gas of molar mass $M$ at temperature $T$:

$v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}},v_{\text{avg}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{8RT}{πM}}$

The ratio is independent of $T$ and $M$:

$\dfrac{v_{\text{rms}}^{2}}{v_{\text{avg}}^{2}}=\dfrac{3π}{8}=\dfrac{3\times 22}{8\times 7}=\dfrac{33}{28}$

Given $\dfrac{v_{\text{rms}}}{v_{\text{avg}}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{α+5}{α}}$:

$\dfrac{α+5}{α}=\dfrac{33}{28}\Rightarrow 28α+140=33α\Rightarrow 5α=140\Rightarrow α=28$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Unpolarised light is incident on the boundary between two dielectric media, whose dielectric constants are 2.8 (medium $-1$) and 6.8 (medium $-2$), respectively. To satisfy the condition, so that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other, the angle of incidence should be $\tan ^{-1}\left (1+\frac{10}{θ}\right )^{\frac{1}{2}}$ the value of $θ$ is $__________$.

(Given for dielectric media, $μ_{r}=1$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a dielectric with $μ_{r}=1$, the refractive index is $n=\sqrt{ε_{r}μ_{r}}=\sqrt{K}$, so $n_{1}=\sqrt{2.8}$ and $n_{2}=\sqrt{6.8}$.

When the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, the angle of refraction is $r=90^{\circ }-i$. Snell's law $n_{1}\sin i=n_{2}\sin r=n_{2}\cos i$ then gives Brewster's condition:

$\tan i=\frac{n_{2}}{n_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{6.8}{2.8}}=\sqrt{\frac{17}{7}}=\left (1+\frac{10}{7}\right )^{1/2}$

So $i=\tan ^{-1}\left (1+\dfrac{10}{7}\right )^{1/2}$, giving $θ=7$.

Hence, the answer is 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
